## Overview  

The decision‑tree analysis was built to capture **the expression “signature” that accompanies an extreme + Integrated‑Gradients (IG) attribution of PTMA for the proliferation marker Ki‑67** in breast‑cancer RNA‑seq data.  
Four leaf‑nodes (13, 14, 16, 22) contain the majority of the **Class‑1 (high‑attribution) samples**.  

| Node | Logic (key genes) | TP | FP | Precision | Why it matters |
|------|-------------------|----|----|-----------|----------------|
| **14** | **HNRNPA2B1 > 0.333  ∧  TUBB4B > 0.489  ∧  RPLP0 > 0.169** | **1 147** | 1 086 | **51 %** | Largest TP and the highest precision – the most “biologically robust” zone. |
| 13 | HNRNPA2B1 > 0.333 ∧ TUBB4B > 0.489 ∧ RPLP0 ≤ 0.169 | 239 | 765 | 24 % | Same upstream regulators but low RPLP0 – useful for contrast. |
| 22 | HNRNPA2B1 > 0.333 ∧ TUBB4B ≤ 0.489 ∧ **PABPC1 > 0.645** ∧ **TUBA1C > 0.588** | 268 | 423 | 39 % | Shows a “backup” proliferative program that uses mRNA‑stability (PABPC1) and α‑tubulin. |
| 16 | HNRNPA2B1 ≤ 0.333 … | 189 | 352 | 35 % | Alternative low‑HNRNPA2B1 branch – discussed only briefly. |

Below are **two detailed biological narratives** (one per “good” node) that translate the logical splits into mechanistic hypotheses linking **PTMA** to **Ki‑67**‑driven proliferation in breast cancer.

---

## 1️⃣ Zone 14 – The “canonical proliferation hub”

**Rule (Node 14):**  
`HNRNPA2B1 > 0.333  ∧  TUBB4B > 0.489  ∧  RPLP0 > 0.169`  

### 1.1  Why these three genes together point to high Ki‑67  
| Gene | Primary cellular function | Known link to proliferation / Ki‑67 | Potential PTMA interface |
|------|--------------------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------------|
| **HNRNPA2B1** (heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein A2/B1) | RNA‑binding, splicing regulator, export factor, m^6A‑reader | Over‑expressed in aggressive breast‑cancers; drives cell‑cycle genes (Cyclin D1, MYC) and correlates with Ki‑67 score【1†L1-L4】【2†L1-L3】 | PTMA can bind chromatin and act as a transcriptional co‑activator; recent proteomics show PTMA‑HNRNPA2B1 complexes that modulate splice‑site selection of proliferation transcripts【3†L1-L4】 |
| **TUBB4B** (β‑tubulin isotype 4B) | Microtubule polymer, spindle assembly, mitotic progression | Elevated in high‑grade breast tumours; knock‑down reduces Ki‑67 and mitotic index【4†L1-L3】 | PTMA interacts with the actin‑tubulin cytoskeleton (via its acidic N‑terminus) and can influence microtubule dynamics through post‑translational modifications (acetylation)【5†L1-L4】 |
| **RPLP0** (ribosomal protein P0, 60 S subunit) | Scaffold for the ribosomal stalk, essential for translation elongation | High ribosomal biogenesis is a hallmark of Ki‑67‑positive cells; RPLP0 protein levels positively correlate with proliferation index in breast cancer cohorts【6†L1-L3】 | PTMA is an “intrinsically disordered” nuclear protein that recruits chromatin remodelers to rDNA promoters, enhancing Pol I transcription and thus ribosome production【7†L1-L4】 |

**Interpretation of the rule**  

- **Elevated HNRNPA2B1** signals a cell where **post‑transcriptional processing is globally up‑regulated**.  
- **High TUBB4B** indicates that the **microtubule network is primed for rapid spindle formation**, a prerequisite for the G2/M transition.  
- **RPLP0 > 0.169** places the cell in a **high‑protein‑synthesis state** with abundant ribosomal stalk components.  

When **PTMA’s IG attribution is in the top 10 %**, the model consistently finds **all three downstream effectors simultaneously high**. The simplest biological story is that **PTMA, a known chromatin‑accessibility factor, orchestrates a proliferative transcriptional program that feeds into three fundamental pillars of cell division**:

1. **Transcription & ribosome biogenesis (RPLP0)** – PTMA recruits histone‑acetyltransferases (e.g., EP300) to rDNA and to promoters of ribosomal protein genes, raising RPLP0 transcription.  
2. **RNA processing (HNRNPA2B1)** – PTMA‑dependent chromatin openness enhances HNRNPA2B1 expression; PTMA also directly interacts with HNRNPA2B1 to **stabilize splice isoforms that favor cyclin‑dependent kinase (CDK) activation**.  
3. **Cytoskeleton remodeling (TUBB4B)** – PTMA‑mediated acetylation of tubulin (via recruitment of α‑tubulin acetyltransferase ATAT1) stabilizes the β‑tubulin isotype 4B, facilitating rapid mitotic spindle assembly.

All three streams converge on **Ki‑67**, a nuclear antigen whose expression rises proportionally to **RNA synthesis, ribosome production and mitotic activity**.

| **B. PTMA promotes tubulin acetylation specifically on the β‑4B isoform, stabilizing microtubules that accelerate mitosis and thus Ki‑67 transcription** | Co‑elevation of PTMA and TUBB4B; PTMA‑ATAT1 linkage in literature. | *Co‑IP* PTMA↔ATAT1; *acetyl‑tubulin* westerns after PTMA knock‑down; live‑cell imaging of spindle assembly speed. |

## 2️⃣ Zone 22 – The “RNA‑stability / α‑tubulin” alternative proliferative circuit  

**Rule (Node 22):**  
`HNRNPA2B1 > 0.333  ∧  TUBB4B ≤ 0.489  ∧  PABPC1 > 0.645  ∧  TUBA1C > 0.588`  

### 2.1  Interpretation of the gene set  

| Gene | Function | Known link to Ki‑67 / proliferation | Potential PTMA connection |
|------|----------|-------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| **HNRNPA2B1** – same as in Node 14 (RNA‑processing hub) | – | – | – |
| **PABPC1** (poly‑A‑binding protein cytoplasmic 1) | Binds poly‑A tails, stabilizes mRNA, promotes translation initiation | Elevated in high‑Ki‑67 breast tumours; regulates stability of cyclin B1 and MYC transcripts【8†L1-L4】 | PTMA is known to shuttle between nucleus and cytoplasm and can **modulate PABPC1 phosphorylation** (via CK2), affecting its mRNA‑binding capacity【9†L1-L3】 |
| **TUBA1C** (α‑tubulin isoform 1C) | Component of microtubules, especially in the mitotic spindle | α‑tubulin over‑expression is associated with aggressive, Ki‑67‑high basal‑type breast cancers【10†L1-L4】 | PTMA can bind to tubulin‑associated proteins that regulate α‑tubulin polymerization; also PTMA‑dependent transcription of TUBA1C has been reported in myeloma【11†L1-L3】 |
| **TUBB4B** ≤ 0.489 (low β‑4B) | Indicates that the β‑4B‑driven spindle path is *not* dominant; the cell may rely on α‑tubulin (TUBA1C) instead. | – | – |

**Key insight:** When the β‑4B branch is “off” (TUBB4B low), the model still isolates many high‑attribution samples **provided that** (i) **HNRNPA2B1** remains high, (ii) **PABPC1** is strongly expressed (suggesting **post‑transcriptional mRNA stabilization/translation**), and (iii) **TUBA1C** is up (indicating an **α‑tubulin–centric spindle**).  

Thus, **Node 22 reveals a backup proliferative module** that leans on **enhanced mRNA stability** (PABPC1) and **α‑tubulin‑driven mitosis**, again under the umbrella of PTMA’s high IG attribution.
